Isogonal Tangents

GeometryCirclesConstructions
Game: Three circles sit in the gaps between three rays from one point, and each ray just touches two circles.
How to play: Drag a coloured point to swing a ray, or focus it and use the arrow keys. Press Show names to label the points and watch where the three new lines meet.
Look for the math

Each ray touches two circles, so it is already one touching line for each pair. Every pair has another one. The surprise is that these three other lines still meet at one point however the rays are swung.

One line, two circles

A line that just touches a circle is a tangent. Our ray runs between the two centres of its pair, so it is an internal tangent. Reflect that ray across the line joining the two centres: each circle keeps its shape under that reflection, so the image is the pair's other internal tangent. The applet draws this one, farther from O, and labels its crossings with the rays A, B and C.

The meeting point

Take the three second tangents two at a time. Their three crossings are concurrent: all three are the same point X, and the applet reports their average to soften drawing errors. This is part of Mannheim's theorem: if one internal tangent from each pair of three circles meets in a point, then the other three internal tangents meet in a point too.

Checked, not just claimed

The logic test compares every constructed point with a second transcription of the applet's bytecode, and checks the page's claims on 360 shapes: each ray touches both circles, each second line is the mirror image of the ray, and the three second lines meet to within 10−6 of the board size. Tangent or nearly tangent circles are reported as unstable instead: when two circles merge at a point the two lines fall together and the crossing is hard to read.

A line in the printed proof

The page quotes Steiner's theorem for the four-sided figures AOBX and AODX. Its second identity is printed as AO + DX = DO + DX, which simply cancels to AO = DO. The step the proof needs is AO + AX = DO + DX; with that correction the transitivity argument gives BO + BX = DO + DX and the proof goes through. The live page now says it needs Sun's Java VM, so this port follows the applet's bytecode for the construction and the page for the claim.

Try swinging a ray until two circles almost touch. Watch the three green crossings pull together, then drift apart again as you pull the ray back.
